page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.large is an x86_64 general-purpose instance built upon the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz, allocating 2 burstable vCPUs across a single physical core with dual threading. Memory capacity stands at 8.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory balance of 4.0 GB per core. The processor incorporates modern compute extensions, including AVX-512, Intel AMX for matrix operations, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES and SHA-NI. The instance includes no local storage and provides a baseline network allocation of 0 Gbps, relying entirely on remote network-attached storage.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a clear divergence between single-core and multi-threaded throughput. Driven by high clock speeds and architectural capabilities, the instance demonstrates strong single-threaded compute efficiency, achieving 2056.0 in Geekbench single-core testing alongside top-quartile execution in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core place in the lower quartile of measured systems, constrained by its single physical core allocation. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 19.96 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 14.37 GB/sec also reflect the limited bus footprint of a smaller slice.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the flex tier couples modern Intel processor capabilities and DDR5 memory with a burstable CPU model, reducing infrastructure expense for systems that do not mandate sustained full-core utilization. The absence of bundled local storage and GPU accelerators keeps resource density focused on lightweight execution. The m8i-flex.large is suited for low-traffic web serving, staging and test environments, background task workers, and small API endpoints.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.large is an entry-tier general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating up to 3.9 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. Configured with 2 burstable vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core and 8 GB of DDR5 memory, it provides a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio without bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for vector and matrix computations. Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance, demonstrated by top-quartile results in Geekbench single-core tests and gzip compression throughput. However, its multi-core output and memory bandwidth fall into lower percentiles due to its single physical core constraint. Offering qualitative cost efficiency for intermittent compute demands, the m8i-flex.large is suited for low-traffic web serving, lightweight microservices, small background workers, and entry-level development environments.
